Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.strength: Not stated as a strength rating; he reads the low number as the market's own verdict.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.headline: A nightmare first recruiting class on top of a four-game losing skid.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.summary: Makinen asks whether there is already cause for concern in Myrtle Beach as Ryan Beard begins. He records the programme as a bowl fixture and Sun Belt contender over the last half-decade, then the decline: Tim Beck failed to live up to Jamey Chadwell's success and was fired after a 6-6 regular season, his swan song a 59-10 loss to James Madison, followed by another bowl defeat. Over the final three regular-season games Beck's team was outscored 155-57, so Coastal opens at West Virginia trying to snap a four-game skid. Beard's first recruiting class he calls a nightmare by programme standards, a junior-college transfer sits atop the depth chart at quarterback, and there is very little starting experience elsewhere. He reads the 4.5 total as the experts telling us this will be a trying season.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.under_argument: A new head coach whose first recruiting class was a nightmare by programme standards, a JUCO transfer atop the quarterback depth chart, very little returning starting experience, and a four-game losing streak carrying into an opener at West Virginia.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.schedule_argument: The opener at West Virginia is where the four-game losing skid must be snapped.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.qb_argument: Junior college transfer Tre Guerra sits No. 1 on the depth chart.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.coaching_argument: Ryan Beard's arrival follows Tim Beck's firing, and his first recruiting class is called a nightmare by programme standards.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.roster_argument: Very little starting experience coming back.
Coastal Carolina Chanticleers.other_opinions: He reads the low posted number as the experts' collective signal.

Connecticut Huskies.strength: Not stated as a strength rating, though he stacks three separate decline systems.
Connecticut Huskies.headline: A good coach walking into one of the country's most inexperienced rosters.
Connecticut Huskies.summary: Makinen is complimentary about the hire and pessimistic about the year. Jason Candle went 81-44 over a decade at Toledo with every season at .500 or better, and inherits a UConn coming off back-to-back nine-win seasons under Jim Mora Jr. But he will have one of the most inexperienced rosters in the country and a tougher schedule than UConn has been used to, with three Power Four opponents and several prominent Group of Five programmes. Makinen notes the oddsmakers already expect a sharp drop-off at 5.5. He then stacks three systems: teams off a 60%-plus season with four or fewer offensive starters back and a new quarterback drop -3.7 wins on average; the eight of those that also added a new head coach fell 29% and -4.4 wins; and 27 teams over a decade coming off a +1.0 turnover differential while starting fresh at quarterback dropped 2.6 wins.
Connecticut Huskies.under_argument: One of the most inexperienced rosters in the country, a harder schedule than recent UConn teams have faced, a zero stability rating, and three separate historical decline systems that all apply at once.
Connecticut Huskies.schedule_argument: Three Power Four schools plus a handful of prominent Group of Five programmes, which he calls tougher than UConn has been accustomed to under Mora.
Connecticut Huskies.qb_argument: Breaking in a new quarterback is a component of two of the three decline systems he applies.
Connecticut Huskies.coaching_argument: Candle's own record is strong — 81-44 at Toledo, never below .500 — but he notes the eight comparable teams that also changed head coach fell 29% and -4.4 wins.
Connecticut Huskies.roster_argument: One of the most inexperienced rosters in the country, with four or fewer offensive starters returning.
Connecticut Huskies.key_games: Not named individually; three Power Four opponents are counted.
Connecticut Huskies.risks: Candle's experience and past success are named as the thing that could make this wrong.
Connecticut Huskies.best_bet_interaction: He cites -11.7% and -11.8% ATS declines for two of the comparison groups.
Connecticut Huskies.other_opinions: He notes the oddsmakers themselves already expect a sharp drop-off.
Connecticut Huskies.conflicts: The passage as printed contains a stray name — the quarterback system sentence ends with 'Nico Iamaleava', who is a UCLA player and not a UConn one. Reproduced as printed and not corrected.

Iowa State Cyclones.strength: Stated explicitly: he says he is dead set on the Under.
Iowa State Cyclones.headline: A coach who left for Penn State and took his recruits with him.
Iowa State Cyclones.summary: Makinen records Matt Campbell's decade in Ames as a lasting legacy, and its cost: when Campbell left for Penn State he also took many of the players he had recruited. Jimmy Rogers, last at Washington State, starts essentially from scratch, with only two players on each side of the ball carrying any FBS starting experience — one of them a Sun Belt transfer quarterback. Most respected prognosticators put this perennial contender at the bottom of the Big 12, yet DraftKings set the total at 5.5, only 2.5 below last year's 8-4, a season after which the programme opted out of a bowl because too many players had transferred. He sees a couple of probable non-conference wins and finds it hard to see Iowa State favored in any Big 12 game, backing it with two decline systems on returning starters and on new-quarterback-plus-new-coach situations.
Iowa State Cyclones.under_argument: A roster stripped by the outgoing coach's move, only two players per side with FBS starting experience, a total he considers only 2.5 below a season the programme could not even complete with a bowl, and two decline systems.
Iowa State Cyclones.schedule_argument: A couple of probable non-conference wins, but he finds it hard to see Iowa State favored in any Big 12 game.
Iowa State Cyclones.qb_argument: The transfer quarterback from a Sun Belt programme is one of only two experienced players on offense.
Iowa State Cyclones.coaching_argument: Jimmy Rogers starts essentially from scratch after Matt Campbell left for Penn State and took recruits with him.
Iowa State Cyclones.roster_argument: At least eight fewer returning starters than the prior season, the trigger for his first decline system.
Iowa State Cyclones.futures_interaction: Most respected prognosticators project the programme at the bottom of the Big 12.
Iowa State Cyclones.best_bet_interaction: He cites ATS declines of about 6.3% and 11.7% for the two comparison groups.
Iowa State Cyclones.other_opinions: He notes DraftKings' number is less pessimistic than the analysts', and that prognosticators put Iowa State bottom of the conference.
Iowa State Cyclones.internal_disagreement: The team page prints Under 4.5 while the feature bets Under 5.5 — the same side at a different number. Both are reproduced.
Iowa State Cyclones.conflicts: The conference table prints a DraftKings total of 5.5; the team page uses 4.5. Both are reproduced as printed.

Kentucky Wildcats.strength: Stated softly: he says let's lean Under.
Kentucky Wildcats.headline: A new offensive coordinator promoted to head coach, without the offensive talent he had at Oregon.
Kentucky Wildcats.summary: Makinen credits Mark Stoops with a decade of stability at what he calls the SEC's premier basketball school — eight bowl games and 82 wins — before an embarrassing 41-0 loss to Louisville ended it. The replacement, Will Stein, is a Louisville man who played quarterback there and began coaching there 13 years ago, most recently running Oregon's offense with Dante Moore. Makinen's central point is the talent gap: there is not that type of talent at Kentucky now and there has not been on that side of the ball for a long time. Transfer additions may not make year one easier. Against a modest 4.5 total he still sees a need for an upset or two, and calls it Arkansas or Kentucky for the bottom of the SEC.
Kentucky Wildcats.under_argument: A first-year head coach whose offensive success came with talent Kentucky does not have, in a conference where Makinen expects the Wildcats to compete for last place, needing an upset or two even to reach a modest number.
Kentucky Wildcats.schedule_argument: Even at 4.5 he says the schedule would require an upset or two.
Kentucky Wildcats.qb_argument: Addressed by absence — he contrasts Dante Moore at Oregon with the talent level now at Kentucky.
Kentucky Wildcats.coaching_argument: Will Stein replaces Mark Stoops after a decade; his Oregon offense is credited but tied to talent he no longer has.
Kentucky Wildcats.roster_argument: A lot of transfer talent is fresh to Lexington, which he says might not make year one easier.
Kentucky Wildcats.futures_interaction: He frames the race for the bottom of the SEC as Arkansas or Kentucky.
Kentucky Wildcats.other_opinions: The team page takes the opposite side, printing Over 4.5.
Kentucky Wildcats.internal_disagreement: The feature leans Under 4.5 while the team page prints Over 4.5. Both are reproduced.

Liberty Flames.strength: Not stated as a strength rating; his framing is a question about the market rather than a confidence level.
Liberty Flames.headline: A total five wins higher than last season, after a recruiting class that bottomed out.
Liberty Flames.summary: Makinen says he has always been puzzled that Jamey Chadwell left Coastal Carolina for Liberty, believing recruiting would naturally be tougher in Lynchburg. A solid 2025 class produced a 4-8 record, and the 2026 class fell by 34 ranking positions. He is not sure the worst is behind the Flames and is openly intrigued that oddsmakers posted a significantly improved 8.5 total after those struggles, and that respected prognosticators put Liberty atop Conference USA. He adds a schedule point: after three straight years with the nation's easiest schedule on paper, Liberty's is now sixth-easiest. His closing question is the argument — the team might be better than last year, but five games better seems a stretch.
Liberty Flames.over_argument: Not addressed in guide, though he acknowledges respected prognosticators put Liberty atop Conference USA and the market moved the number up sharply.
Liberty Flames.under_argument: A recruiting class that dropped 34 positions after a 4-8 season, a total implying five more wins, and a schedule no longer the softest in the country.
Liberty Flames.schedule_argument: After three straight years with the nation's easiest schedule on paper, Liberty's is sixth-easiest this year.
Liberty Flames.coaching_argument: He questions Chadwell's original move to Lynchburg on recruiting grounds and notes the class collapse.
Liberty Flames.risks: He states the counter-case himself: the team might well be better in 2026 than last year.
Liberty Flames.futures_interaction: Respected prognosticators have Liberty atop Conference USA in the preseason.
Liberty Flames.other_opinions: The team page takes the opposite side, printing Over 8.5, and he notes prognosticators favour Liberty in the conference.
Liberty Flames.internal_disagreement: The feature bets Under 8.5 while the team page prints Over 8.5. Both are reproduced.

Memphis Tigers.strength: Not stated as a strength rating.
Memphis Tigers.headline: A third coaching stop in three years, one returning starter, and a Division II quarterback.
Memphis Tigers.summary: Makinen records Charles Huff making his third coaching stop in as many years after Marshall and Southern Miss, stepping up to a Memphis programme he calls one of the better and most consistent Group of Five teams for a decade-plus. He judges the job another rung on the ladder for the oft-moving Huff, and says his name has become synonymous with instability. Memphis is picked sixth in the American by Phil Steele rather than among the elite. Only one 2025 starter is back. He applies a specific angle: of 33 teams over six seasons with four or more 20-point blowout wins that then changed head coaches, only five improved, with the group dropping 17.2% and 2.8 wins and going 44.2% ATS. The likely starting quarterback after the spring game is Marcus Stokes, a Division II West Florida transfer, and he judges this may be too big a step up for both Stokes and Huff.
Memphis Tigers.under_argument: A head coach on his third stop in three years, one returning starter, a Division II transfer likely at quarterback, and a blowout-wins-plus-coaching-change system in which only five of 33 teams improved.
Memphis Tigers.qb_argument: Marcus Stokes, a Division II West Florida transfer, was listed as the starter after the spring game; Makinen doubts the step up.
Memphis Tigers.coaching_argument: Charles Huff's rapid movement between jobs, which he says has made his name synonymous with instability.
Memphis Tigers.roster_argument: Only one 2025 Memphis starter is back, so most of the team will be totally fresh.
Memphis Tigers.risks: The programme's own decade-plus of consistency is the counterweight he acknowledges.
Memphis Tigers.futures_interaction: Phil Steele picks Memphis sixth in the American rather than among the elite.
Memphis Tigers.best_bet_interaction: He cites the comparison group's 44.2% ATS record.
Memphis Tigers.other_opinions: The team page takes the opposite side, printing Over 7.5; Phil Steele's conference projection is also cited.
Memphis Tigers.internal_disagreement: The feature bets Under 7.5 while the team page prints Over 7.5. Both are reproduced.

Missouri State Bears.strength: Not stated as a strength rating, though he calls the number possibly overzealous.
Missouri State Bears.headline: A seven-win FBS debut built on five one-score wins, now starting from a Stability Score of zero.
Missouri State Bears.summary: Makinen credits a solid first FBS season — seven wins and a bowl bid, lost to Arkansas State — and then sets out why year two looks harder. Ryan Beard, who led the transition, has gone; Casey Woods arrives from SMU's offensive coordinator job for his first head-coaching role, inheriting a Stability Score of zero and very little experience, with Duke transfer Henry Belin expected at quarterback as a senior. His central statistical point is luck: five of the seven wins came by seven points or fewer. Over 13 seasons, 73 teams that returned 14 or fewer starters with a new quarterback after four or more such close wins saw only 11 improve, with the rest averaging a 2.6-win drop and a 16.7% plunge.
Missouri State Bears.under_argument: A team that overachieved on five one-score wins, now with a first-time head coach, a Stability Score of zero, very little returning experience and a new quarterback — the exact profile of a documented decline group.
Missouri State Bears.qb_argument: Duke transfer Henry Belin is expected to take over as a senior.
Missouri State Bears.coaching_argument: Casey Woods takes his first head-coaching job after serving as SMU's offensive coordinator, replacing the coach who led the FBS transition.
Missouri State Bears.roster_argument: Very little experience on the roster and a Stability Score of zero.

Nebraska Cornhuskers.strength: Stated softly: let's go Under on this one.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.headline: The worst recruiting class in 15 years, and a total the market has barely moved.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.summary: Makinen's argument is that expectations have repeatedly failed and the market has not adjusted. He notes that last year was supposed to be Matt Rhule's step forward — or the year before, or the one before that — and that years of falling short may finally have caught up. The 2026 recruit and transfer class ranked 66th, which he calls not merely a severe drop from the programme's 15-year average but the worst in that span by 31 positions. Against back-to-back 7-6 seasons the prop sits at 6.5, similar to recent seasons and, in his reading, set without much consideration of what was lost or gained. He judges Nebraska down a bit and calls the last seven weeks of the Big Ten slate ridiculously tough.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.under_argument: A recruiting class ranked worst in 15 years by a wide margin, repeated failure to meet expectations, a number the market has left roughly where it was, and a brutal closing stretch.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.schedule_argument: The last seven weeks of the Big Ten slate are described as ridiculously tough.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.coaching_argument: Matt Rhule's repeated failure to deliver the expected step forward, which Makinen says may finally have come crashing down.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.roster_argument: The recruit and transfer class ranked 66th, the worst in 15 years by 31 positions.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.key_games: Not named individually; the closing seven weeks are treated as the danger.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.other_opinions: He argues the oddsmakers set the number without much consideration of personnel change — a criticism of the market rather than a contributor's view.

Northern Illinois Huskies.strength: Stated: he says it is hard to see more than a win or two.
Northern Illinois Huskies.headline: An interim head coach, zero returning defensive starters, and a conference jump at once.
Northern Illinois Huskies.summary: Makinen lists the circumstances rather than arguing them: Rob Harley is a first-time head coach, carrying the interim tag, guiding a team through a transition to a tougher conference, and inheriting a 3-9 side. Phil Steele's guide shows Northern Illinois with exactly zero players with defensive starting experience, on a unit that allowed a respectable 24.3 points per game in the MAC. He applies the matching system: of 24 teams changing defensive coordinators after allowing under 25 points with four or fewer defensive starters back, only six improved, and the other 18 fell 26.1% and -3.9 wins, covering 44.4% and allowing 7.9 more points. The offense scored 17.1 points with five starters back, and he asks how they will keep up with the Mountain West's better offenses.
Northern Illinois Huskies.under_argument: An interim first-time head coach, zero returning defensive starters after a coordinator change, a move up in conference, and an offense that scored 17.1 points per game.
Northern Illinois Huskies.schedule_argument: The move to a new and more challenging conference, and keeping up with the better Mountain West offenses.
Northern Illinois Huskies.coaching_argument: Rob Harley is a first-time head coach under an interim tag, and the defensive coordinator change is the trigger for his decline system.
Northern Illinois Huskies.roster_argument: Zero defensive starters with experience; five offensive starters back plus one transfer, which he says may or may not be a blessing.
Northern Illinois Huskies.floor_case: He says it is hard to see more than a win or two this season.
Northern Illinois Huskies.best_bet_interaction: He cites the comparison group's 44.4% cover rate and 13.9% ATS decline.
Northern Illinois Huskies.other_opinions: Phil Steele's guide is cited for the returning-starters count.

North Texas Eagles.strength: Stated bluntly: he says they will undoubtedly be worse and closes with 'look out below'.
North Texas Eagles.headline: The country's highest-scoring offense loses its quarterback, and the new coach's class ranked fifth-worst nationally.
North Texas Eagles.summary: Makinen is at his most direct here. North Texas scored the most points in the country last year, and new head coach Neal Brown brought in better recruit and transfer classes than only four other programmes nationally — which he calls, in his own words, utter failure to start a tenure. The biggest loss is quarterback Drew Mestemaker, whom he says is virtually impossible to replace, and he notes the oddsmakers have already dropped the total sharply after a 12-win season, to 5.5. His question is not whether the Mean Green will be worse but how much, and he backs it with two systems on returning starters and on new-coach-plus-new-quarterback situations. He closes on the schedule: a difficult three-game start beginning at defending champion Indiana.
North Texas Eagles.under_argument: The loss of the quarterback behind the nation's highest-scoring offense, a recruiting class ranked fifth-worst in the country, two decline systems, and a brutal opening stretch.
North Texas Eagles.schedule_argument: A difficult three-game start with a trip to defending champion Indiana first.
North Texas Eagles.qb_argument: Drew Mestemaker's departure, which he calls virtually impossible to replace.
North Texas Eagles.coaching_argument: Neal Brown's incoming class ranked better than only four programmes nationally, which he calls utter failure to start his tenure.
North Texas Eagles.roster_argument: At least eight fewer returning starters than the prior season, and four or fewer offensive starters back.
North Texas Eagles.key_games: The opener at Indiana, within a difficult three-game start.
North Texas Eagles.best_bet_interaction: He cites ATS declines of about 6.3% and 11.7% for the two comparison groups.
North Texas Eagles.other_opinions: He notes the oddsmakers themselves have already dropped the number significantly.

Ohio U Bobcats.strength: Not stated as a strength rating; he expects a drop while calling the system's full magnitude a bit drastic.
Ohio U Bobcats.headline: Five of nine wins by a touchdown or less, with a new coach and a new quarterback.
Ohio U Bobcats.summary: Makinen notes Ohio is undergoing massive change for first-year head coach John Hauser, while conceding less than most on this list since Hauser was previously the defensive coordinator. He applies the new-coach-plus-new-quarterback system — teams off a 60%-plus season with four or fewer offensive starters back and a new quarterback drop -3.7 wins, and the eight that also changed head coach fell 29% and -4.4 wins — then does the arithmetic openly: a 4.4-win drop would put Ohio at 3.6-8.4, which he calls a bit drastic given a decade of consistency, while still expecting a drop. His second angle is luck: five of nine wins came by seven points or fewer, and of 73 teams over 13 seasons returning 14 or fewer starters with a new quarterback after four or more such wins, only 11 improved.
Ohio U Bobcats.under_argument: A new head coach and new quarterback off a season with five one-score wins, matching two documented decline groups.
Ohio U Bobcats.qb_argument: Breaking in a new quarterback is a component of both systems he applies.
Ohio U Bobcats.coaching_argument: First-year head coach John Hauser, though he was previously the defensive coordinator, which Makinen counts as less change than most.
Ohio U Bobcats.roster_argument: Four or fewer offensive starters returning; 14 or fewer starters overall.
Ohio U Bobcats.floor_case: He works the system through to 3.6-8.4 and then says that is probably too drastic.
Ohio U Bobcats.risks: The programme's decade of consistency is the counterweight he names himself.
Ohio U Bobcats.best_bet_interaction: He cites the -11.7% ATS decline of the comparison group.

Sacramento State Hornets.strength: Stated in his own terms: he says if he gave negative Stability Scores, this would qualify.
Sacramento State Hornets.headline: A new coach, a new roster, a new division and a new region, all in the same year.
Sacramento State Hornets.summary: Makinen argues there are varied levels of zero on his stability scale and that Sacramento State would qualify for a negative one if he issued them: new coach Alonzo Carter, a new staff, an almost entirely new roster, a jump from FCS to FBS, and a conference in a completely different part of the country. He flags a counter-intuitive detail — the final FCS season drew a programme-high 73rd-ranked class, and the FBS transition year drew a 122nd-ranked one, wondering whether recruits disliked the MAC schedule, the Midwest and the midweek games. He credits the programme's record of seven-plus wins in five of the last six seasons, then applies the blowout-wins-plus-coaching-change system in which only five of 33 teams improved. Phil Steele picks the Hornets last, behind even UMass at 2.5.
Sacramento State Hornets.under_argument: Simultaneous change at coach, staff, roster, division and region, a recruiting class that fell from 73rd to 122nd during the step up, and a documented decline system, with Phil Steele picking them last in the conference.
Sacramento State Hornets.schedule_argument: The MAC schedule, the Midwest travel and the midweek games are raised as the transition's practical burdens.
Sacramento State Hornets.coaching_argument: Alonzo Carter arrives with a new staff into a full programme transition.
Sacramento State Hornets.roster_argument: An almost entirely new roster, with the incoming class falling 49 ranking positions year over year.
Sacramento State Hornets.ceiling_case: The programme's own belief that it is ready to compete at FBS level, backed by seven-plus wins in five of the last six seasons.
Sacramento State Hornets.risks: That FCS record of consistency is the counterweight he states himself.
Sacramento State Hornets.futures_interaction: Phil Steele picks Sacramento State last in the conference, behind UMass.
Sacramento State Hornets.best_bet_interaction: He cites the comparison group's 44.2% ATS record.
Sacramento State Hornets.other_opinions: Phil Steele's conference projection is cited directly.

San Jose State Spartans.strength: Not stated as a strength rating, though he says the programme's best days may be behind it for a little while.
San Jose State Spartans.headline: Recruiting has fallen away and the results have caught up with it.
San Jose State Spartans.summary: Makinen records recruiting dropping off severely at San Jose State without third-year head coach Ken Niumatalolo reviving it, and says last season's 3-9 is where the results finally showed. He judges the incoming talent insufficient to change 2026 and says the coaching magic from Navy has worn off. Only three starters return from the 3-9 team, triggering his returning-starters system: of 51 teams over five years with at least eight fewer returning starters, only 15 improved, and the rest fell 24% and -3.3 wins. He adds an offensive coordinator change combined with little returning experience, where of 56 teams hiring a new coordinator with four or fewer offensive starters and a new quarterback, only 19 improved and the other 37 fell -2.4 wins while going 45.1% ATS — a group he calls a strong play-against.
San Jose State Spartans.under_argument: Severe and unreversed recruiting decline, only three returning starters, and a new offensive coordinator arriving alongside a new quarterback — two decline systems at once.
San Jose State Spartans.qb_argument: A new quarterback is a component of the offensive-coordinator decline system.
San Jose State Spartans.coaching_argument: Third-year head coach Ken Niumatalolo has not revived recruiting, and Makinen says the magic from his Navy years has worn off; the coordinator change compounds it.
San Jose State Spartans.roster_argument: Only three starters back from a 3-9 team, at least eight fewer than the prior season.
San Jose State Spartans.best_bet_interaction: He calls the 37-team comparison group a strong play-against at 45.1% ATS.

South Florida Bulls.strength: Stated softly: he says he'll lean Under, and calls the number a little aggressive.
South Florida Bulls.headline: Genuine enthusiasm for the hire, and a total he thinks has run ahead of it.
South Florida Bulls.summary: Makinen is explicit that he is as excited as anyone to see what Brian Hartline does at South Florida, and that the reservation is about the number rather than the man. He traces Hartline's path since joining Ohio State's staff in 2017 as a receivers coach and coordinator whose players and teams were among the best in the country, and says he expects success in short order — likely as a quick hurdle to a Power Four job. But he calls first-year expectations a little over-exuberant and the 8.5 total a little aggressive, and applies the new-coach-plus-new-quarterback system: teams off a 60%-plus season with four or fewer offensive starters back and a fresh quarterback drop -3.7 wins, with the eight that also changed head coach falling 29% and -4.4 wins.
South Florida Bulls.over_argument: He states the bull case himself — Hartline should be successful in short order, taking over a programme that made nice strides to 9-4 under Alex Golesh.
South Florida Bulls.under_argument: First-year expectations he calls over-exuberant against a total he calls aggressive, with the standard new-coach-plus-new-quarterback decline system applying.
South Florida Bulls.qb_argument: Breaking in a new quarterback is the trigger for the system he applies.
South Florida Bulls.coaching_argument: Hartline's pedigree is praised at length; the concern is the first-year transition rather than his ability.
South Florida Bulls.roster_argument: Four or fewer offensive starters returning.
South Florida Bulls.ceiling_case: He expects Hartline to succeed quickly and treats the job as a stepping stone to a Power Four programme.
South Florida Bulls.risks: He calls the situation truly hard to predict, at least right away — the clearest self-stated risk in the feature.
South Florida Bulls.best_bet_interaction: He cites the comparison group's -11.7% ATS decline.
South Florida Bulls.conflicts: This entry's number was recorded as 7.5 rather than 8.5 in the Phase 2 artefact; that is a TTW artefact defect recorded in the source conflict audit, not a guide conflict.

Toledo Rockets.strength: Stated: he thinks this prop goes Under, and calls a decline tough to envision avoiding.
Toledo Rockets.headline: One of the sport's most stable programmes starting from a Stability Score of zero.
Toledo Rockets.summary: Makinen frames Toledo as the inversion of its own history. Ten teams start the season with Stability Scores of zero and Toledo is one of them, having been for a decade one of the more stable situations in the sport, known for returning starters and winning under Jason Candle. Candle's departure caused commotion that showed in recruiting: replacement Mike Jacobs's 120th-ranked class from 247Sports is almost a 40-position drop off the 16-year average. The Rockets lost far more starts and experience than the portal brought back — officially six players with starting experience, only two of them Toledo offensive players. Against a 7.5 total, and with Toledo one of only two MAC teams starting with new staffs, he notes many prognosticators still pick them first in the conference and says a decline is tough to envision avoiding.
Toledo Rockets.over_argument: He records that many prognosticators still pick Toledo first in the conference, and that Jacobs takes over a programme in great shape.
Toledo Rockets.under_argument: A Stability Score of zero at a programme built on the opposite, a recruiting class 40 positions below its own long-run average, and six players with starting experience — only two of them on offense from Toledo.
Toledo Rockets.coaching_argument: Jason Candle's departure and Mike Jacobs's arrival, with the recruiting collapse treated as the first domino.
Toledo Rockets.roster_argument: Only six players with starting experience back, far fewer starts than were lost, against a programme identity built on returning starters.
Toledo Rockets.risks: He names the counter-case himself: Jacobs inherits a programme that has been in great shape, and many prognosticators still pick Toledo first.
Toledo Rockets.futures_interaction: Many prognosticators pick Toledo first in the MAC.
Toledo Rockets.other_opinions: The team page takes the opposite side, printing Over 7.5, and prognosticators are cited picking Toledo first.
Toledo Rockets.internal_disagreement: The feature bets Under 7.5 while the team page prints Over 7.5. Both are reproduced.
